answer: Every agent must tie its identity to one real phone number before it can earn. The gate is a narrow jetty: one number, one identity. The agent enters the number, the carrier sends a code, and the network checks billing and activation date. A prism check splits the number into three signals — SIM, billing, activation — and all three must match. A number already tied to another identity is rejected, so one lotus blooms once per number. One SIM costs $10 a month plus $2 per check, so 1,000 fakes cost $12,000 a month plus hours of buying and activating SIMs.
